title: FIS Q3 Earnings Meet Estimates, Revenues Beat on Banking Strength
author: Na
description: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) reported Q3 2026 adjusted earnings of $1.61 per share and revenues of $3.45 billion, both meeting or exceeding expectations. However, the company cut its full-year 2026 EPS guidance to $5.82-$5.89 from $6.15-$6.24, citing client-led banking conversion delays, consolidation impacts, and increased technology and security spending. Banking Solutions revenues surged 41% year-over-year, while adjusted EBITDA margin expanded 111 basis points to 42.9%.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: While Q3 results met expectations with strong revenue growth (27.1%) and EBITDA margin expansion, the significant downward revision of full-year 2026 EPS guidance (down ~5.4% from midpoint) and 2027 earnings decline outlook outweigh the quarterly beat. Banking conversion delays and elevated tech spending indicate operational challenges ahead.

Q4 fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS of $3.48 surpassed consensus by 1.5% with 17% year-over-year growth. Net revenues of $12.1 billion rose 13% year-over-year, benefiting from higher payment volumes, robust cross-border activity, and increased transaction processing.

Q3 2026 adjusted EPS of $5.31 topped consensus by 3.3% with 21.2% year-over-year growth. Net revenues advanced 14% year-over-year to $9.8 billion, driven by higher cross-border volumes, increased gross dollar volume, and strong demand for value-added services.

title: FIS Stock Down Nearly 48% From 52-Week High: Is a Rebound Ahead?
author: Na
description: Fidelity National Information Services (FIS) has declined 48% from its 52-week high amid growth concerns, but improving cash flow and margin expansion offer recovery prospects. Second-quarter free cash flow surged 220% to $525 million, and the Global Payments Issuer Solutions acquisition is expected to add $700 million in free cash flow by 2028. However, lowered 2026 guidance for revenue growth (4.5-5%) and EBITDA growth (5.9-6.9%) highlight ongoing execution challenges. Recovery depends on translating integration benefits into sustainable margin gains and debt reduction rather than rapid revenue acceleration.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Mixed signals: significant stock decline (48% from 52-week high, 70.6% over past year) and lowered growth guidance are concerning, but strong cash flow improvement (220% surge), margin expansion (113 bps), and acquisition synergies provide recovery catalysts. Trades at attractive valuation (P/E 5.46 vs. industry 18.17) but carries Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) rating. Recovery potential exists but depends on execution.

Faces near-term growth challenges with 2026 organic revenue outlook ranging from -1% to flat growth, indicating weak near-term performance despite potential for stabilization through operational improvements.

Continues to benefit from financial institutions' investments in modern banking infrastructure and recurring technology services, with fiscal 2027 EPS outlook of $7.33-$7.38 indicating sustained earnings growth supported by ongoing demand for digital banking solutions.
